assets.event: The brown planet of Haons hangs in deep space with its two moons; the promise: here one can ascend as a god.
The final gateway: colossal pillars of blue lightning tear through a storm-lit mountain pass, a trial of several hundred billions of volts.
Lightning floods the gateway — only divine-level beings could withstand this power.
A dark-haired man in a white commander's coat descends through the gateway storm, arms spread wide, shards orbiting him.
Ray's face in extreme closeup, eyes glowing white, teeth gritted as he declares he only needs to pass this gateway to stand on top of the world.
Ray bellows his challenge into the Valley of Volts as blue lightning splits the dark rocks around him.
Anuth, the vice master, watches unseen from behind the valley boulders, a blade ready.
A giant bolt of lightning slams down before Ray on his rock spire while the watcher's pale hand creeps into the frame.
Anuth charges through the storm with his knife drawn, closing on the distracted master.
The blade bursts through Ray's body in a spray of blood, the death-blow streaking the frame.
Ray's eyes flash red with rage as the blade sits inside him, the vice master's head looming at his shoulder — unclear: whose shocked line 'WHAT IS...!'.
The master's body drops hard onto the cracked wet rock, blue light still spitting across the ground.
A colossal pillar of lightning erupts through the valley, blasting the sfx-lit air white.
Beneath the light storm, Anuth looms tall over Ray's bleeding, kneeling back.
Ray, blood at his lips, recognizes his betrayer — 'Urk!' — wide-eyed disbelief as he clutches his chest.
Anuth, calm behind his dark visor among the storm clouds, gloats that he can tell Ray didn't expect this.
Ray glares bloodshot and snarling through bloodied teeth — 'I trusted you...' — the betrayal raw on his face.
Ray screams in agony inside a bordered frame, red eyes blazing, blood flying.
Anuth seizes Ray by the collar amid the lightning, sneering that trash shouldn't pretend to be the master.
A hand snatches at Ray in a burst of blue energy — the core soul being torn toward the traitor.
Anuth runs Ray through from behind on grey speed lines — don't worry, Haons will take good care of this body.
Ray's face in framed closeup, mouth bloodied wide in a death-agony scream.
unclear: dark stone behind a burst of flying blood — the dying strike's punctuation.
Anuth grins with glowing eyes, golden lightning crackling — the core soul is in his hands, and now he is the master of Haons.
Ray's broken body lies on the wet stone while the traitor turns away holding the stolen core soul.
The dying Ray's eye rolls back, blood at the corner of his mouth — you're going to regret this, I'll make sure of it.
The valley's lightning erupts sky-wide as a dark figure is hurled down the slope by the blast — unclear: whether the storm is reclaiming the gateway or striking the thief.
unclear: a light-haired young man winces, gloved hand shielding his eyes from the light — an unseen witness to the master's fall.
A sunlit blue sky over a multi-story school building and fence — a bright, ordinary world far from Haons.
A bruised red-eyed young man lifts his head off the floor — huh?
The dark-haired boy in a school uniform sits slumped against a green wall, lost — where am I?
He touches his own bruised face in disbelief — I'm still alive?
Cho Hee Sung, the brown-haired school bully, laughs over the unconscious boy with two flunkies — knocked out after one hit.
A fist seizes the boy's collar and hauls him close — hey, Kang Tae Wook.
The bully yanks Tae Wook up by his collar, glaring down at him.
Cho Hee Sung's smirking sneer up close — tell me if you wanna die, I'll do you that favor any time.
Classmates watch from their desks — he's bullying Kang Tae Wook again; guess he provoked Cho Hee Sung and got it coming.
A fist rockets toward the viewer in a burst of red — the bully swings at the helpless boy.
A hand catches the fist mid-strike, fingers clamping around it — the punch simply stops.
Tae Wook holds the captured fist without a flicker, eyes cold under his hair — who the f*ck are you to get all up in my face?
Face to face: Tae Wook's red eyes glint icy and amused while the bully's rage shakes him.
The captured arm bends the wrong way with a crack, light bursting around the joint.
Cho Hee Sung's face contorts in a scream as his arm gives.
With a concussive burst Tae Wook hurls Cho Hee Sung away across the classroom, arm still outstretched.
Cho Hee Sung tumbles through the air, all four limbs wheeling.
Cho Hee Sung slams back-first into the green chalkboard wall and crumples.
Cho lies crumpled over a desk among the front rows as the whispers spread — he took him down in one blow?
Tae Wook allows himself a small, satisfied smile in profile.
Cho Hee Sung's gang looms over a beaten, glasses-wearing boy painters-green with dread on the floor.
The bruised glasses-wearing boy pleads — just apologize to Cho Hee Sung, else you're in big trouble.
Tae Wook stands before a boiling blue-black nebula, wind in his hair, recognition dawning.
In a washed-out memory, three suit-clad bullies kick a boy on the floor of his home.
A masked boxer throws a punch beside a young martial-arts doctor — the two branches of human training.
A kneeling healer channels pale light into her palm, the great hall glowing gold around her.
A burning orange nebula carries the system's law — water, fire and lightning classes, rated one to twelve stars.
The past master stands arms loose in a shaft of light, golden rings of aura coiling around him — master of both medicinal arts and martial arts.
Close on his torso as the golden rings tighten — the body of a man both healer and fighter.
Back in the present: the bruised student surveys the room beneath a freezing blue nebula of thought — his aura gone, his core soul sealed.
In the classroom, Tae Wook grips his own blood-red tie, resolve hardening — he'll dig up the secrets of his father's death.
The transfer student stands against icy blue smoke, bruise on his cheek, stare like a drawn blade — just you wait, Anuth.
Cho Hee Sung kneels trembling against the wall while Tae Wook looks down at him — that bastard made his past life miserable.
Tae Wook extends his hand down to the beaten boy — get up, I don't need to take sh*t from them.
Tae Wook looks almost gentle in a blue-halftone portrait — a warm-up is just right.
Over Cho Hee Sung's shoulder: Tae Wook cracks his knuckles and smiles — how long are you gonna stay down?
Cho stares hollow-eyed and bloodied, unable to process the boy in front of him.
Tae Wook's face splits into a predatory grin, red eyes gleaming — why, you scared?
Cho shrieks at his frozen lackeys — what the hell are you standing there for, get him!
Tae Wook's red-eyed glare from below — ah, you're going to come all at once?
The lackeys panic and wave each other off — you go first! / why should I go first?!
Cho Hee Sung's face twists with rage against a blue halftone — I told you to take him down!
The gang charges over blue speed lines with chairs raised as Tae Wook turns to meet them head-on — and the swing comes whistling down.

pipeline_note: FILM-FORMAT reader draft for chapter-01 (test run). Identity notes: the white-coat master is RAY (past-life self of Kang Tae Wook, named by the in-page caption card at 7190-7570). The dark-gear traitor is ANUTH ('Vice master', named by the in-page caption card at 10590-10835; bible lists 'Anuth - In Haons' and the ch01 stabber matches). The brown-haired school bully is CHO HEE SUNG (named by a classmate's bubble at ~63300). The glasses-wearing friend is SUH JAE DONG (named by Ray's recognition bubble at ~83750). The light-haired witness after the blast (asset 27) is NEW and unidentified. Twist for harmonization: Ray returns to 'the high school I attended on Earth' and suspects he came back in time - his memories show Earth schoolboy years, bullied, father died. Watermarks sit INSIDE art at 9490-9580, 30740-30840, 36480-36560, 40190-40270, 75850-75950, 83460-83555, 106630-106710; every crop boundary abuts or dodges them. ~12 tiles carry slivers of speech bubbles sliced by frame edges (their text is washed white downstream and folded into the adjacent asset's event) - deliberate trade to keep subjects whole; worst cases: asset 4 (shout bubble tail), asset 29 (HUH bubble), asset 49 (flanked by two bubbles). Title card at 54330-55100 (logo + 제1화) excluded per packaging rule. Ambiguous lines folded with 'unclear:' flags: 'WHAT IS...!' (asset 10), the blood splash (asset 22), the post-blast valley convulsion (asset 26), the 'AH... SH*T...' beat (106730-107580, folded into asset 60's exclusion). Alternative to note: asset 25 (dying face) is a narrow 345-wide inset kept as a 0.86 window crop; a slow creep-pan over the full 39010-39740 inset would also read well if the assembler supports narrow pans. Chapter ends mid-brawl (swarm charge) with no resolution beat - cliffhanger by design.
